text.en: A connecting wire is made of copper but the heating element of an iron is made of nichrome. Both are metals, yet the choice is not random; it depends on a number called resistivity.

Experiments show that the resistance R of a conductor is directly proportional to its length L and inversely proportional to its area of cross section A.
Writing this as an equation gives R = rho L / A, where rho is a constant for the material called its electrical resistivity or specific resistance.
Rearranging, rho = R A / L, and if L = 1 m and A = 1 square metre then rho = R.
So resistivity is the resistance of a conductor of unit length and unit area of cross section, and its unit is ohm metre.
Resistivity measures the resisting power of a specified material to the passage of current and is a constant for a given material, unlike resistance, which also depends on the size of the wire.
The reciprocal of resistivity is the electrical conductivity, with the unit ohm to the minus one metre to the minus one, also called mho per metre.
Conductivity is a measure of the ability of a material to pass current, and the conductance G of a conductor is the reciprocal of its resistance, G = 1/R.
Good conductors such as copper and aluminium have low resistivity, for example copper 1.62 x 10 to the minus 8 ohm metre.
Insulators such as glass and rubber have enormously high resistivity, from 10 to the 10 up to 10 to the 16 ohm metre.
Conductivity is more for conductors than for insulators, but resistivity is less for conductors than for insulators.
Nichrome has a high resistivity of about 1.5 x 10 to the minus 6 ohm metre, so it is used for heating elements.
Doubling the length of a wire doubles its resistance, while doubling its cross-sectional area halves the resistance.

problem.en: A wire 10 m long has resistance 2 ohm and cross-section 2 x 10^-7 m2. Find its resistivity, conductance and conductivity.

text.en: Resistivity rho = R A / L = 2 x 2 x 10^-7 / 10 = 4 x 10^-8 ohm m.
Conductivity = 1 / rho = 1 / (4 x 10^-8) = 0.25 x 10^8 = 2.5 x 10^7 mho per metre.

prompt.en: Explain how resistance depends on length and area, and how resistivity differs from resistance.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking resistivity changes with the length of the wire

points.en: R = rho L / A; R grows with length and falls with area.
Resistivity (ohm metre) is a property of the material; conductivity is 1/rho.
Conductors have low resistivity; insulators have very high resistivity.
Nichrome is used in heaters because of its high resistivity.
